name: Conant Hall
use: Offices, including TRIO Scholars (relocating); historically chemistry, later Psychology
architect: Construction supervised by Randlett of Dow & Randlett (archives spell it 'Daw and Randlett')
statusNote: Phase 1 closure list, Oct 2025; TRIO relocating

renovations.what: Extensive renovation for the Psychology department; rededicated May 9, 1986

facts.text: One of the original buildings of the 1893 move from Hanover; named for John Conant, a farmer who gave $70,000 for buildings and scholarships.
Home of chemistry from 1893 to 1929 and headquarters of the American Chemical Society from 1907 to 1911.
Designated a National Historic Chemical Landmark on Oct. 29, 1999, the first in New England, for Charles James's rare-earth separation work done there.
UNH's university architect said Conant has 'a lot of net asset value'; closing it would allow a comprehensive renovation later.

verdict: 1893 original with an ivy-covered crenellated front and a National Historic Chemical Landmark inside, now emptied for closure.
notes: The old data's 'HIGH net asset value' matches TNH's quote. Closure execution unconfirmed. No licensed modern photo; ref-01 (archives) shows an ivy-covered brick front with an arched entry. The 1909 and 1901 historic images are small views. 1990s 'essentially ADA compliant' claim from old data not verified.
judgeNotes: Archives photo shows a handsome brick front; only historic licensed images. Function low as it is being vacated. A modern licensed view of Conant's arched entrance (lettered "CONANT HALL") exists at the right edge of murkland-hall/01.jpg (Olivier Aumage, CC BY-SA 2.0 fr); a crop of it would make a better lead than the 1909 view.
